title: Nanoleaf panels might soon work with the Philips Hue app
summary: One less smart lighting app to fuss with.
body: TL;DR Newly leaked images show that Philips Hue could soon release an adapter to integrate Nanoleaf Shapes lights. This info comes after an icon depicting hexagonal wall lights was found in the Hue app. The adapter will purportedly cost about €40 in Europe and may go on sale in September. Back in June, a Philips Hue user spotted that the app had added a new light type icon for hexagonal panel lights that looks more than a little like lights offered by Nanoleaf. At the time, we assumed that meant that Hue was cooking up its own hexagonal panel lights — but now, it looks like the icon may actually have been Nanoleaf lights, after all. Smartlights.de has shared some information about an unannounced “wall light module” from Philips Hue. The report says that Hue will release a kind of adapter for Nanoleaf’s Shapes lights that’ll let users integrate the third-party wall lights into existing Hue setups.

title: Karol G, Judeline & Rusowsky Take ‘BbY WOW’ To No. 1: ‘So Thankful’
summary: "I’m so thankful to Karol for giving me this opportunity," says Judeline on their first No. 1.
body: Judeline and Rusowsky score their first Billboard No. 1, as “BbY WOW,” with Karol G , rockets from No. 5 to the top of the Hot Latin Songs chart (dated Aug. 29). “BbY WOW” lands at No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs — which blends streams, airplay and sales — off a streaming-fueled surge. The collab registered 6.1 million official on-demand streams in the United States during the Aug. 14-20 tracking week, according to Luminate. The sum takes the song to a No. 34 start on the overall Streaming Songs chart and to an equal 5-1 trek on the Latin Streaming Songs list. “It’s honestly hard to believe that a song we recorded just last month is already topping the charts — and in the U.S. of all places,” Judeline shared with Billboard . “Everything around ‘BbY WOW’ has happened so fast that I’m still processing it. I’m so thankful to Karol for giving me this opportunity, and to everyone who has embraced the song. Seeing how far it has traveled in such a short time is something I never could have imagined.” Related Xavi Is First to Lead These 3 Latin Airplay Charts Simultaneously in 2026 Karol G Floods Hot Latin Songs Chart With ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’ No Regrets, Jus…

title: Forever No. 1: Shelley Fabares, ‘Johnny Angel’
summary: When she dethroned Connie Francis, it marked the first time female singers had back-to-back No. 1s on the Hot 100.
body: Forever No. 1 is a Billboard series that pays special tribute to the recently deceased artists who achieved the highest honor our charts have to offer — a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 single — by taking an extended look back at the chart-topping songs that made them part of this exclusive club. Here, we honor the late TV star Shelley Fabares, whose “Johnny Angel” reached No. 1 in April 1962. “Johnny Angel” is so innocent, so chaste, that it immediately conjures a simpler time. It has that in common with such other defining hits of the era as The Chordettes’ “Mr. Sandman” (1954) and The Teddy Bears’ “To Know Him, Is To Love Him” (1958). “Johnny Angel” is a classic “crush” song, in which the singer pines about a boy who is utterly oblivious:”Johnny Angel, how I love him/ He’s got something that I can’t resist/ But he doesn’t even know that I exist.” Related Gone But Not Forgotten: Musicians We Lost in 2026 Forever No. 1: Connie Francis, ‘My Heart Has a Mind of Its Own’ Forever No. 1: Connie Francis’ ‘Everybody’s Somebody’s Fool’ Singer and actress Shelley Fabares , who died on Sunday (Aug. 23) in Los Angeles at a…

title: Frustrating Google Home bug refuses to add items to your shopping lists in Keep
summary: Another day, another Google Home bug.
body: TL;DR Some Google Home users are facing a bug where the voice assistant refuses to add items to their Google Keep lists. While not all users appear to be facing this issue, it appears widespread enough for Google to take notice. Meanwhile, a quick look at Google Home settings suggests that access to notes & lists using a voice assistant may have been removed. It feels like we’re reporting on a Google Home bug or a fix almost every other day. Only today, users received some good news following reports of devices refusing to set alarms over voice commands. Sadly, those good times aren’t going to last, and it now looks like yet another function is being impacted by a similar glitch, as some people are seemingly unable to add items to their lists on Google Keep using Google Home voice commands. In a series of complaints on Reddit, including one from Friday, a user claims the voice assistant recognizes their commands perfectly well, but refuses to add items to the list . For instance, if the person asks one of their Google Home devices to “add x to list xyz,” the assistant might respond by saying how many items are on that list, while refusing to add any new items.

title: Is Digi-Pop the Newest Hyperpop Wave?
summary: How Pupsies' debut chart hit "Misery" could be leading the charge.
body: What’s initially most striking about Pupsies’ “Misery” is the song’s sonics: a buzzing, blaring, synth-bass hum matched with a lo-fi melody that could soundtrack an 8-bit video game. While Pupsies’ favorite part kicks in later — a dramatic, crunchy guitar hook from co-producer Goetia that accompanies her wailing vocal climax — it’s this early, beatless section that helped the song take off on TikTok. Cindy Kamgaing, the 19-year-old from North Carolina better known as Pupsies, has been building an internet following since 2023 for her kinetic, therapeutically revealing digi-pop jams, but had yet to really unlock a mainstream crossover until “Misery.” Following its March release, the emotionally overflowing (but “cute”-­sounding, as Kamgaing proudly puts it) single went viral, taking off with animation edits (like a Steven Universe one that Kamgaing found particularly delightful), and with users jokingly referring to it as a “LARP” song (an abbreviation that traditionally means live action role playing but has come to refer to anyone seen as playing a specific part). “I think people started saying it because the song is kind of like, ‘I’m depressed, I’m a girl,’” Kamgaing says. title: Poll shows plenty of Pixel 10 Pro owners are skipping the Pixel 11 Pro
summary: Annual upgrades continue to lose their shine, even for Pixel owners.
body: It’s certainly tempting to upgrade the moment your smartphone’s successor is released. It’s a feeling that many Pixel 10 and older owners likely felt and are still feeling this week, given that the Pixel 11 series is now available. However, as strong as that temptation might be, it’s often far smarter to resist it. This rings true for Pixel 10 Pro owners in particular, a phone that still has plenty going for it. A little over a year into its lifespan, it can look forward to some six years of software support; its cameras remain some of the best in the game; and it likely won’t slow to a crawl in any noticeable way in the coming months or years.

title: Super Smash Bros. is ready for its unofficial Android port
summary: You can't play it on Switch, but unsanctioned Android ports could be coming soon.
body: TL;DR Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 has been fully decompiled, opening the door to unofficial native ports. The 1999 platform fighter hasn’t been available through official means for several years and isn’t currently playable on Nintendo Switch consoles. We aren’t aware of any ports made from the newly decompiled code yet, but we expect they’ll start appearing soon. Aside from some high-profile rereleases, present-day Nintendo is notoriously stingy when it comes to providing easy, legitimate access to its immense back catalog of classic games. This, in part, has inspired fans to take matters into their own hands by decompiling old favorites, recreating their source code so the games can be easily (if unofficially) ported to modern platforms like Windows or Android. Now, another classic that’s been inaccessible on modern hardware is ripe for porting: 1999’s Super Smash Bros. has been fully decompiled. As shared on Decomp.dev , Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 64 is now “100.00% decompiled,” meaning the game’s source code has been completely recreated and it’s ready to be ported. Compared to emulated games, ports created from decompiled source code can run natively on modern hardw…

summary: Listening area in Google Translate may offer extensive control over the Live Translate feature for Android XR-based devices.
body: TL;DR Google Translate could introduce big Live Translate updates for the Android XR platform. Last year, we uncovered development on Live Translate for Google’s extended reality platform. We can now exclusively reveal a potential feature addition for the Live Translate experience on Android XR. You’re reading an Authority Insights story. title: The next wide-screen foldable may have just leaked in real-world images
summary: New leaked images offer a closer look at Xiaomi’s mysterious wide-screen foldable.
body: TL;DR Xiaomi’s next foldable has leaked, showing a wide inner display and a design that closely resembles the company’s own HyperOS 4 teaser. The XRing O3 will power the device, with a 10-core CPU, Arm’s new G2-Ultra NX GPU, and eye-catching performance claims. The Xiaomi 18 Fold launches in September, but key details such as global availability, pricing, and dimensions remain unknown. Xiaomi’s XRing O3 chipset has already made headlines with some seriously ambitious performance claims, but the chip’s first phone may be just as interesting. Xiaomi has confirmed that the 3nm processor will debut in the Xiaomi 18 Fold next month, and now leaked images appear to show the company’s upcoming foldable in the flesh. The images, which Digital Chat Station (DCS) shared on Weibo , show a book-style foldable with a wide inner display similar to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 , relatively thick bezels, and a punch-hole selfie camera near the upper-right corner. One image also shows the rear of the device, including a large camera module, but it doesn’t reveal enough to say much about its hardware.

title: New leak suggests Qualcomm’s next Snapdragon 8 Elite could take it to the extreme, literally
summary: Qualcomm's naming convention is getting further out of hand.
body: TL;DR According to a new leak, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip will be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. It could feature two prime cores clocked at 5.01GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. The Dimensity 9600 Pro could also use two prime cores clocked at 4.55GHz, along with three performance and three efficiency cores. Qualcomm and MediaTek are both gearing up to launch their latest flagship processors. The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 series and the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro are expected to feature improvements across the board. Now, a new leak is shedding some light on the core arrangement and clock speeds of the top-of-the-line Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and the Dimensity 9600 Pro. According to a Weibo post by Digital Chat Station (DCS), the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro, model number SM8975, could be called the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 instead. The extremely long (pun intended) and unnecessarily weird name notwithstanding, Qualcomm’s next flagship chip seems set to break the 5GHz barrier for smartphone chipsets.

title: Galaxy S26 series gets sixth One UI 9 beta release, but when is the stable update coming?
summary: The latest 851MB update targets several UI and routine issues for global users ahead of the stable launch.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung has released the sixth One UI 9 beta for the Galaxy S26 series. The 851MB update (firmware ZZHE) includes the August 5, 2026, security patch and fixes key issues, including display errors with the Now Brief widget and photo-saving issues in Expert RAW 24MP at specific focal lengths. Currently live in Germany, India, Poland, the UK, and South Korea, the new update will soon be available in the US as well. Samsung entered One UI 9 development with much gusto, but after releasing the stable update alongside the new Galaxy Z8 foldables, the pace of One UI 9 beta releases for its previous flagships has slowed down a bit. After releasing the fifth One UI 9 beta almost two weeks ago, Samsung is now picking things up with the sixth One UI 9 beta release for the Galaxy S26 series. We’ve received the sixth One UI 9 update on our Galaxy S26 Ultra in the UK. This Android 17-based update comes with firmware version ending in ZZHE, the August 5, 2026 security patch, and is 851MB in size.

title: 5 reasons I may not go back to Spotify after trying YouTube Music
summary: YouTube Music isn't perfect, but you can't ignore the value proposition.
body: As is the case with millions of users around the world, I’ve been a loyal Spotify subscriber for as long as I can remember. The app works well across Android and iOS, there’s a great selection of music, and features like Jam and Spotify Connect have made my listening experience much more seamless across audio devices at home. I was happy to pay for the Premium Duo plan — until it was sneakily taken away. Spotify removed the Duo plan in India around November 2025, but as I had subscribed to it long before, I was able to continue with it, as it should be. Then came the email, one July morning this year, saying my Premium Duo plan was canceled due to an “issue” with my payment method. Nothing had changed, so it didn’t make any sense. I figured it was Spotify forcing me to upgrade to a higher-priced plan, and as it turned out, I wasn’t the only one who got the boot. Frustrated with this move, I decided to try other options.

title: After just 5 days, my Pixel 11 Pro is already a brick
summary: This isn't a great start.
body: The Pixel lineup and hardware woes seem to go hand in hand. Whether it’s OLED tint issues with the Pixel 2 XL, overheating, spontaneously shattering camera glass, or display issues with the Pixel 9 Pro lineup, hardware troubles seem constant. As a day-one Pixel user ever since the first phone launched, I’ve usually been immune to all the troubles that tend to plague Google’s flagship. Well, as the saying goes, luck eventually does run out. I’ve had my Pixel 11 Pro for just five days, and it’s already a brick. A couple of days into my time with the Pixel 11 Pro (in the gorgeous Canyon colorway), I decided to do a factory reset and a fresh setup instead of copying over all my data from my previous phone, and here we are.

title: The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a camera problem, and it has nothing to do with photo quality
summary: Samsung put the Galaxy Z Fold 8's folding display selfie camera in the worst spot.
body: I’ve spent years trying the latest book-style foldables, but none earned a permanent spot in my pocket once I finished testing them. Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 7 came the closest with a thin-and-light design and truly flagship specs. Unfortunately, it suffered from the same problems as every other folding phone with a squarish inner screen aspect ratio. The form factor isn’t conducive to widescreen video content, as you’ll see large black bars at the top and bottom of the folding screen. Samsung built the wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 to specifically address this pain point, and it quickly won me over. Then, something happened that I didn’t expect. I found myself using the Galaxy Z Fold 8 unfolded in portrait orientation more than landscape.

title: Sony’s new phone is one of your only options with microSD support, but it’s not all roses
summary: Hey Sony, how about upgrading something?
body: TL;DR The Xperia 10 VIII is official with the exact same hardware as the Xperia 10 VII. It comes with the Snapdragon 6 Gen 3, 8GB of RAM, and 128GB of storage. The cameras are also exactly the same as the Xperia 10 VII, and the display is 50% brighter. After a couple of leaks , Sony has finally announced the new Xperia 10 VIII, and it’s basically the same phone as the Xperia 10 VII, bar one small upgrade and a new paint job. The Xperia 10 VIII looks almost exactly the same as the Xperia 10 VII. There’s the horizontal camera bar on the back, “Sony” branding on the camera island, and a front that looks remarkably out of date with thicker bezels on the top and bottom. It also retains the fingerprint scanner and the 3.5mm headphone jack, and Sony claims that the stereo speakers are now 30% louder.

title: We tried Gemini’s new Device Help feature on the Pixel 11, and the results were mixed
summary: Gemini is ready to fix your Pixel, well, almost ready.
body: TL;DR Gemini’s experimental Device Help feature is appearing in the Gemini app on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro devices, letting you troubleshoot your phone using natural language. It can diagnose battery and Wi-Fi issues, open specific settings, change things like brightness and dark mode, and explain Pixel features without making you hunt through Settings. It’s still a Labs feature and can get things wrong. Our testing produced inconsistent instructions for Magic Capture, so it isn’t completely reliable yet. A few days ago, we spotted Google testing a clever new Gemini trick that could save Pixel users from digging through the Settings app every time something goes wrong. That feature, called Device Help, is now appearing directly inside the Gemini app on some of our Pixel 11 series devices. First spotted by 9to5Google , Device Help is currently showing up on Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro models we’ve checked, including our Pixel 11 Pro XL units. It still has a “Labs” badge attached, though, which is Google’s way of telling you things may not always work as expected. And after putting it through a few tests, that’s exactly what we found.

title: Google’s Tensor G7 has one last chance to save the Pixel 12
summary: Dubious silicon is detracting from Pixel's best features.
body: The Pixel 11 series has left Google with something of a dilemma. Based on our time with the phones so far, they remain among the most enjoyable Android handsets to use, thanks largely to Google’s software experience and a growing collection of genuinely useful features. But our testing of the Tensor G6 shows that Google’s custom silicon is falling further behind rival flagship chips; early gaming tests suggest a familiar litany of issues; and a week with the Pixel 11 Pro suggests that many of Google’s newest AI tricks aren’t yet strong enough to make up the difference. That’s not necessarily a problem for the Pixel 11, but it could become one for the Pixel 12.

title: Spotify has good news if your audiobooks suddenly stopped playing
summary: But some are still unable to play chapters despite the reported fix.
body: TL;DR Spotify experienced an outage that prevented listeners from playing or downloading audiobooks across multiple devices. The issue has officially been marked as resolved, though a few users report that playback glitches remain. Users still affected should update the app and report the issue on the Help board. Spotify has been steadily adding more reasons to spend time with audiobooks, from narrated magazine articles to TV-style recaps and Playlist Notes . But today, some listeners were unable to play those audiobooks at all, and Spotify now says the problem has been fixed. The issue surfaced earlier today, with Reddit reports coming from users across phones, desktops, and the web. Spotify acknowledged the problem through its Community forum, saying it had received reports that audiobook playback was not working properly and that the relevant teams were working on a fix.

The feature is designed to reduce motion sickness by displaying motion cues on the screen while you’re in a moving vehicle. Motion Assist is available through Google Play Settings and can automatically activate in a moving vehicle or be controlled manually through a Quick Settings tile. Google is gradually rolling out its new Motion Assist feature on Android 17 , starting with Pixel phones. The feature helps users reduce motion sickness when using their phones in a moving vehicle. title: Spotify bug leaves Android Auto drivers staring at error message
summary: Spotify not working for you on Android Auto? You're not alone.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Android Auto users are reporting issues with Spotify. The app is displaying an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” It’s unclear what the cause of the problem is. Sometimes being an Android Auto user can feel like playing a game of whack-a-mole. A bug appears, a fix is rolled out, and another bug appears shortly after. For example, a fix for a glitch that caused connections to drop or freeze was recently released . Now, a new bug has shown up, and it’s preventing users from streaming their music and podcasts. According to several Android Auto users on Reddit ( 1 , 2 ), the latest issue affects the Spotify app. When attempting to access the app, these users are running into an error message that reads “Spotify isn’t responding.” The screen includes options to exit the app or to wait for it to start working again.

title: The Pixel 11 Pro XL is built to last and easy to fix, teardown finds
summary: It's pricey, but at least you'll be able to hold onto it a few years.
body: TL;DR JerryRigEverything’s Zack Nelson has tested the Pixel 11 Pro XL’s durability and repairability. The phone didn’t bend in Nelson’s durability test, and key components are relatively simple to swap out. Nelson calls the Pixel 11 Pro XL “one of the easiest phones to repair of 2026.” It looks like it should be relatively easy to make the Pixel 11 Pro last. The XL version has now undergone the JerryRigEverything treatment, and the phone held up nicely to Zack Nelson’s usual battery of abuse. The teardown video also shows that common repairs should be relatively simple, with both the display and the battery removable with just a few minutes of work. The video shows that the 11 Pro XL barely bends or flexes at all as Nelson wrenches on it, so the phone should hold up fine in case you sit down with it in your back pocket. Despite Google’s claim that the 11 Pro’s display is “more than twice as scratch-resistant than previous models” thanks to a new coating, though, it still scratches at level six with deeper grooves at a level seven.

title: Netflix is reportedly in talks to add rival streamers like Peacock
summary: Netflix could soon open up its service to other streamers.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Netflix could soon let you access other rival streamers through its platform. The company is reportedly in talks with Peacock and Fox One. It’s unclear if Netflix would sell subscriptions to those streamers or just include their content directly in the app. From Peacock to ESPN , there’s been a rash of streaming-related price hikes lately. If you’re worried that this article will be about Netflix announcing a rate increase, you can rest easy. That’s not happening, at least not yet anyway. Rather, this has to do with Netflix reportedly opening up its service to its rivals. It appears that Netflix is interested in becoming a one-stop shop for streaming. title: Chrome’s new rules ruined ad blockers. Here are 4 things that still work
summary: You can still block ads — just not how you used to.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority A few years ago, Chrome introduced Manifest V3 and began phasing out the older Manifest V2 technology used by some of the most advanced browser extensions. According to Google, the older version was harder to maintain and had its own real security risks, but we suspect it’s also because Google wanted to rein in extension capabilities. Unfortunately, this also made it harder to install extensions like the highly popular uBlock Origin. While workarounds still existed by using Chrome flags, that’s no longer the case . It is now virtually impossible to get MV2 extensions to work in Chrome.

title: Crazy report reveals Exynos 2700 could outperform Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro
summary: Just FYI, Samsung reportedly conducted these tests itself.
body: TL;DR Samsung reportedly tested its Exynos 2700 chip against the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Gen 6 Pro. According to the tests, the Exynos 2700 performed 9.5% better than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 in Geekbench 6.5. It also performed 5% better in gaming and 24% better in gaming under low-power conditions. It’s no secret that the Exynos 2700 is coming and will power many phones in the upcoming Galaxy S27 series , at least in some regions. However, if you’re wondering whether an Exynos chipset in your next Galaxy flagship means poor gaming performance and thermal throttling, Samsung may have good news. According to a report from South Korean outlet SEDaily , citing industry sources, the Exynos 2700 outperformed the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro in an in-house evaluation by Samsung. The report further claims that the Exynos chip beat Qualcomm’s Snapdragon chip in multiple categories.
